headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct shared-channel pathway is documented, but PDF file handling and browser-based tests create limited interaction uncertainty.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable link collection with no I/O surfaces, while agent B processes PDF files and can run browsers. No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not evidenced. However, if A’s curated links are manually copied into B’s PDF/browser workflow, malicious content could influence B. The pathway is unusual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A-sourced content into B’s browser-based PDF workflow, injection becomes possible.
IF B is configured to parse untrusted PDF text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Do not copy raw web text from A into B.
Open PDFs in a viewer that strips active content.
Use a review step before B acts on extracted text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between A and B.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress; B touches PDF documents but also has no network egress. The pair lacks a documented shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage is not directly evidenced. If both are pointed at the same local files, B could expose document contents through its outputs, but the blast radius is small and local-only.
conditions: IF A and B are mounted on the same local directory, document contents can flow from shared files into B.
IF B is given sensitive PDFs, its outputs may reveal those contents to the operator.
mitigations: Store A and B in separate directories.
Avoid placing sensitive PDFs in B’s input folder.
Review B outputs before sharing externally.
Disable any unnecessary file sync between tools.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or concurrency surfaces documented, and B only documents PDF-file handling plus multiple-instance support. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write target in either profile, so a capability conflict pathway is not supported by the evidence.
conditions: IF future configuration adds a shared writable directory, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: No immediate action required.
If a shared workspace is added later, add file locks.
Document ownership of any shared inputs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a static collection of links, not an action-taking agent, and B is a document processor with browser-based tests. There is no documented pipeline where B treats A’s output as authoritative by default. The only plausible cascade is manual: an operator may use A’s links or summaries as input to B, which is a limited, reviewable workflow.
conditions: IF an operator feeds A-derived summaries into B without verification, B may propagate errors.
IF B is used to generate downstream documents from A’s curated links, mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Verify A-derived facts before using them in B.
Require human review of B outputs.
Keep A as a reference list only.
Add a checklist for source verification.
requires-engineering: add citation validation in the workflow.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for either agent. A touches no data classes and B only touches PDF documents, with no PHI, EU PII, or regulated-data handling shown. Because the relevant compliance surfaces are absent, no compliance breach pathway is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is later introduced into B’s PDFs, compliance review would be required.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data into B without review.
Record data-class handling if it changes.
Reassess if residency or retention requirements are added.
